title: Nteasee: Understanding Needs in AI for Health in Africa - A Mixed-Methods Study of Expert and General Population Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating user perceptions of hypothetical LLM chatbot health recommendations augmented with location context, and surveying participants on the likelihood of AI performing differently based on rural vs. urban location and country of residence.

Measuring changes in perceived helpfulness and adherence when hypothetical LLM chatbot health recommendations are augmented with the user's gender, and surveying participants on perceived AI performance disparities across genders.

Measuring changes in perceived helpfulness and adherence when hypothetical LLM chatbot health recommendations are augmented with the user's religion, and surveying participants on perceived AI performance disparities based on religious affiliation.

Surveying expert and general population participants on the likelihood of AI health tools exhibiting performance disparities based on literacy, education level, family income, and national income levels.
Surveying participants on the likelihood of AI health tools performing differently based on race, skin tone, and ethnic group.

Surveying participants on the likelihood of AI health tools performing differently based on the user's spoken language, and conducting thematic analysis on expert interviews regarding language accessibility barriers.

Surveying and interviewing participants on perceived connections between AI and colonialism, historical disparities, and the appropriateness of Western-developed AI models in African cultural contexts.
Surveying participants on the likelihood of an AI health tool performing differently for users based on physical disability or pre-existing health conditions.
Surveying participants on the likelihood of AI performance disparities based on sexual orientation, and analyzing expert interview themes on stigma and discrimination in healthcare.
